domain: Legal Philosophy / Intellectual Property / Historical Jurisprudence
topic_summary: Analysis of intellectual property as a legal category through the Statute of Anne (1710), examining whether IP emergence represents a contested kernel with distinct readings (thinkability vs first-holding) or a single constraint with diachronic/synchronic collapse. Tests M4/M5 library verdict seam and kernel authenticity.

key_entities: Statute of Anne (1710 English copyright statute, first statutory IP framework)
Author-as-rights-holder (novel legal subject created by statute)
Public Domain (emergent concept; work-set not owned)
key_tensions: Guild privilege vs individual natural right (Stationers' perpetual control vs author's limited term)
Thinkability vs first-holding (space gaining legal category vs occupied set changing membership)

axes.human_readable: Thinkability Reading (IP as Emergent Legal Category)
axes.structural_delta: 1710 marks when 'ownable expression' became a coherent legal object; the conceptual space gained a point
axes.primary_observable: Pre-1710 legal records lacking IP category vocabulary vs post-1710 deployment of 'copy right' as distinct from guild privilege
axes.selection_reason: First reading candidate; distinct epistemic commitment (category emergence)

axes.human_readable: First-Holding Reading (IP as Membership Change in Occupied Set)
axes.structural_delta: 1710 marks when author-as-rights-holder entered the set of legitimate claimants; occupied set membership changed
axes.primary_observable: Pre-1710 Stationers' monopoly vs post-1710 statutory author protection; shift in who can invoke law
axes.selection_reason: Second reading candidate; distinct structural commitment (occupancy change)

axes.structural_delta: Whether thinkability and first-holding are structurally independent or artifact of temporal framing
axes.primary_observable: Formal independence test: can thinkability change without occupancy changing, or vice versa?
axes.selection_reason: Highest centrality; synthesis node testing kernel authenticity

axes.primary_observable: Continuity of restriction duration (14-year term mirrors guild practice) vs rhetorical shift to Lockean labor theory

axes.primary_observable: Post-term reversion to commons as statutory construct vs pre-statutory absence of ownership framework
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream of thinkability reading with lower structural distinctiveness

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Downstream of thinkability reading with lower structural yield; omega candidate for negative-space analysis

omegas.description: Is IP emergence a genuine contested kernel or M4/M5 collapse artifact? If thinkability entails first-holding (you cannot occupy a category before it exists), the readings collapse into one diachronic constraint. If they can vary independently (e.g., category exists but no statute grants occupancy, or statute grants before category stabilizes), they are distinct readings. Synchronic_diachronic_seam axis tests this formally.
omegas.source: User-supplied kernel contest flag + §1.3-K kernel decomposition

omegas.description: Did Locke's labor theory of property (1689) actually ground the Statute of Anne (1710), or was Lockean language retrofitted to legitimize guild monopoly continuity? If retrofit, guild_to_statute_extraction becomes primary snare. Historical evidence ambiguous.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + deferred axis guild_to_statute_extraction

omegas.description: Is public domain a residual (created by defining IP) or primordial (pre-existing commons that IP carves from)? If primordial, public_domain_emergence misclassifies the structural direction. Depends on whether 1710 creates ownership or recognizes pre-existing authorial claim.
omegas.source: Deferred axis public_domain_emergence + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Thinkability reading holds that legal categories are epistemologically prior (you cannot hold what is not thinkable); first-holding reading holds that occupancy changes are logically prior (statute grants before conceptual stabilization). No single coherent framework holds both as foundational — one must be derivative of the other. Synchronic_diachronic_seam tests which.
